olumo-rock.comment: Climbing to the summit gave me goosebumps! The panoramic view of Abeokuta with the rusty brown roofs and the Ogun river snaking through is unbelievable. The local guides are exceptionally knowledgeable about the 19th-century Dahomey war history.

A true fortress of heritage. We visited with our school excursion group and the sacred shrines carved into the ancient rock caves are breathtaking. The elevator is also convenient for elderly visitors.
Very serene early in the morning before the noon heat. Make sure to wear sturdy sneakers. The cultural dancers at the base were fantastic!

ake-palace.comment: Meeting the royal palace historians was the highlight of our trip. The crown room and historical photo archives dating back to the 1800s capture the true grandeur of Egba civilization.
Incredible royal architecture right in the center of Ake. Peaceful courtyards and deep cultural reverence.

itoku-market.comment: The scent of genuine indigo dye is everywhere! Watching the master dyers stamp intricate cassava starch patterns on cotton was mesmerizing. Bought 3 pieces of authentic Adire Eleko at great prices.
A photographer’s paradise. Vibrant indigo fabrics billowing in the breeze and friendly artisans eager to explain each traditional symbol.

oopl.comment: World-class museum complex! The presidential archives, bamboo park, and wildlife park make this a full-day experience for families.
Modern, well-maintained, and very educational. The artificial lake boat ride in the evening is delightful.

amala-shitta.comment: Best Amala in Ogun State! Piping hot, fluffy black amala served with steaming gbegiri and ewedu topped with tender goat meat and orisirisi.
